subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should browser routes deliberately return the stale acted-on target and require fresh tab selection whenever continuity cannot be proven, rather than preserving any heuristic continuation behavior?
rationale: This is an externally observable browser-route recovery contract with compatibility consequences; the patch can enforce either choice mechanically, but maintainers must choose the permanent public behavior.

options.title: Adopt stale-target fail-safe
options.body: Preserve the acted-on target when no backend-owned successor is available, after fixing serialization and proving the live extension pairing path.

options.title: Specify another recovery contract
options.body: Define an owner-supported continuity mechanism before merge if stale target responses are not the desired caller contract.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Defer the change if the browser contract cannot be approved with a compatible recovery path.

recommendation.title: Adopt stale-target fail-safe
recommendation.body: Preserve the acted-on target when no backend-owned successor is available, after fixing serialization and proving the live extension pairing path.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report and the PR discussion both position steipete as the browser-contract decision owner.
